title: The kb-census skill drives a census through census.py run, groups, brief, apply and finish instead of step-by-step commands
goal: kb-census SKILL.md's phases 0, 1 and 3 are one command each (census.py run, census.py finish), phase 2 builds each subagent's brief with census.py brief and applies its result with census.py apply, the hand steps those replace (grouping, composing the brief, kbid.py add per row, editing _gaps.md and _conflicts.md, census.py record, re-anchoring, the index) are gone from the skill, and the skill tells the orchestrator to read census.py summary's queue block before phase 2 and report it; the kb-census rule sets in kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv still pack good for each phase, with rows reworded or added where a rule moved into a command, and rag.py eval passes on them; the skill's text shrinks, measured with wc -c before and after and given in the commit body.
notes: Consumers of census.py (git grep -ln census.py over .claude, AGENTS.md, .claude-plugin and _tools on 2026-10-10): .claude/skills/kb-census/SKILL.md (this story) and the kb-census rule sets in kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv (this story); _tools/factdiff.py, provider.py, providers.csv (ST-v3pruppq, ST-ai2xlm7x); _tools/ql_capture.py (ST-w3jhowin), ql_distill.py and querylog.py name it in command classification and need an edit only if a new subcommand must be classed apart, which ST-w3jhowin's work checks. AGENTS.md maps to the skill but names no census command, so it is reviewed, not edited (its 4 KB cap). The rule questions of the sets are reworded only where a rule moved into a command, never to make a row pass.
